claim: Pili are critical in host recognition, colonization and biofilm formation during bacterial infection.
source: Pili are critical in host recognition, colonization and biofilm formation during bacterial infection.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific knowledge about pili function.

claim: The crystal structure of SafD-dsc was determined to 2.2 Å resolution.
source: The crystal structure of SafD-dsc was determined by molecular replacement using AfaD (PDB code: 2IXQ) as search model. The final model was refined to 2.2 Å resolution using program PHENIX.REFINE (Adams et al., 2010) (Table 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental crystallographic data showing the resolution achieved.

claim: The crystal structure of SafDAA-dsc was determined to 2.8 Å resolution.
source: The structure of SafDAA-dsc was determined to 2.8 Å resolution by X-ray crystallography.
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental crystallographic data showing the resolution achieved.

claim: SafD and SafA are both required for host recognition.
source: Cell adherence assays show that SafD and SafA are both required for host recognition, suggesting a poly-adhesive mechanism for Saf pili.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell adherence assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: SafDAA-dsc structure reveals an unexpected inter-molecular oligomerization.
source: Moreover, the SafDAA-dsc structure, as well as SAXS characterization, reveals an unexpected inter-molecular oligomerization, prompting the investigation of Saf-driven self-association in biofilm formation.
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data and SAXS analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Structure-based mutants targeting the inter-molecular hydrogen bonds and complementary architecture/surfaces in SafDAA-dsc dimers significantly impaired the Saf self-association activity and biofilm formation.
source: Structure-based mutants targeting the inter-molecular hydrogen bonds and complementary architecture/surfaces in SafDAA-dsc dimers significantly impaired the Saf self-association activity and biofilm formation.
evidence: This is supported by mutagenesis experiments and biofilm formation assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Bacterial cells in a biofilm can become more resistant to most antimicrobial agents and host defenses than their planktonic counterparts.
source: Bacterial cells in a biofilm can become more resistant to most antimicrobial agents and host defenses than their planktonic counterparts (Burmølle et al., 2010; Mah and O'Toole, 2001; Prosser et al., 1987).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Biofilm development can be mainly described in three stages including attachment, maturation and dispersion.
source: Biofilm development is a dynamic progress, and it can be mainly described in three stages including attachment, maturation and dispersion (Rabin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Pili-mediated attachment to the mucosal epithelial layers in human is often thought to be the first step to enable initial contact, to form a microcolony, to carry out invasion and to evade the host immune system.
source: For bacterial pathogenesis, the pili-mediated attachment to the mucosal epithelial layers in human is often thought to be the first step to enable initial contact, to form a microcolony, to carry out invasion and to evade the host immune system that lead to acute and chronicle infections (Proft and Baker, 2009; Sauer et al., 2000; Zavialov et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Bacterial pili can participate in cell-cell interaction, leading to bacterial aggregation and micro-colony formation.
source: In addition, it has been reported that bacterial pili can participate in cell-cell interaction, leading to bacterial aggregation and micro-colony formation (Lo et al., 2013; Wright et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, type I pili are necessary to establish initial attachment with the epithelium, while at least three other types of fimbriae (Lpf, Pef and Tafi) are required for cell-cell interaction, micro-colony growth and biofilm maturation.
source: As demonstrated in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, type I pili are necessary to establish initial attachment with the epithelium, while at least three other types of fimbriae (Lpf, Pef and Tafi) are required for cell-cell interaction, micro-colony growth and biofilm maturation (Ledeboer et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Salmonella enterica is a Gram-negative and food-borne enteric pathogen that is a common cause of human and animal abdominal complications like typhoid fever and gastroenteritis.
source: Salmonella enterica, a Gram-negative and food-borne enteric pathogen, is a common cause of human and animal abdominal complications like typhoid fever and gastroenteritis (Silva et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature and represents established knowledge.

claim: Salmonella enterica can be subdivided into seven subspecies, designated as I, II, IIIa, IIIb, IV, VI and VII.
source: It can be subdivided into seven subspecies, designated as I, II, IIIa, IIIb, IV, VI and VII (Reeves et al., 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Over 99% clinical isolates belong to Salmonella enterica subspecies I, which account for most Salmonella infections in humans and animals.
source: Over 99% clinical isolates belong to Salmonella enterica subspecies I, which account for most Salmonella infections in humans and animals (Folkesson et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Most serotypes of Salmonella enterica are able to form biofilms, which significantly increase their survival in a variety of environments and hosts, and enhance resistance to multiple antimicrobials.
source: Most serotypes of Salmonella enterica are able to form biofilms, which significantly increase their survival in a variety of environments and hosts, and enhance resistance to multiple antimicrobials (Papavasileiou et al., 2010; Sheffield et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Saf pili are often found in clinical isolates of Salmonella enterica.
source: Saf pili are often found in clinical isolates of Salmonella enterica (Folkesson et al., 1999; Townsend et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The saf operon is located on Salmonella enterica centisome seven genomic island.
source: The saf operon is located on Salmonella enterica centisome seven genomic island (Folkesson et al., 2002), which consists of four contiguous genes encoding the major subunit (SafA), periplasmic chaperone (SafB), outer membrane usher (SafC) and minor subunit (SafD) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature and is illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The saf operon consists of four contiguous genes encoding the major subunit (SafA), periplasmic chaperone (SafB), outer membrane usher (SafC) and minor subunit (SafD).
source: The saf operon is located on Salmonella enterica centisome seven genomic island (Folkesson et al., 2002), which consists of four contiguous genes encoding the major subunit (SafA), periplasmic chaperone (SafB), outer membrane usher (SafC) and minor subunit (SafD) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Saf pili are assembled by the chaperone-usher (CU) secretion pathway.
source: Saf pili are assembled by the chaperone-usher (CU) secretion pathway (Remaut et al., 2006; Zavialov et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The nascent SafA and SafD subunits are transported from the cytoplasm into the periplasm via the SEC machinery.
source: The nascent SafA and SafD subunits are transported from the cytoplasm into the periplasm via the SEC machinery (Stathopoulos et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The periplasmic chaperone, SafB, donates its G1 strand to complete the correct folding of SafA or SafD.
source: The periplasmic chaperone, SafB, donates its G1 strand to complete the correct folding of SafA or SafD. Hence, this process is also known as donor strand complementation (DSC) (Choudhury et al., 1999; Sauer et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In the DSE step of Saf pili assembly, the N-terminal extension (Nte) of an incoming SafA replaces the chaperone G1 strand (in SafB) via a zip-in-zip-out mechanism.
source: In the DSE step of Saf pili assembly, the N-terminal extension (Nte) of an incoming SafA replaces the chaperone G1 strand (in SafB) via a zip-in-zip-out mechanism (Remaut et al., 2006; Rose et al., 2008), giving rise to a remarkable polymer of SafD-(SafA)n (n > 100).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SafA subunit and SafB chaperone have been characterized by X-ray crystallography and EM single particle analysis.
source: Concerning the structures in Saf pili, SafA subunit and SafB chaperone have been characterized by X-ray crystallography and EM single particle analysis (Remaut et al., 2006; Salih et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SafD, a putative adhesin/invasin, was demonstrated to have vaccination potential in mice model.
source: SafD, a putative adhesin/invasin, was demonstrated to have vaccination potential in mice model (Strindelius et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Previous studies showed that Saf pili are required for Salmonella infection against pig.
source: As for biological functions of Saf pili, previous studies showed that Saf pili are required for Salmonella infection against pig (Carnell et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Genetic knockout of SafA in S. typhimurium showed little difference in mouse virulence when compared to wild-type Salmonella strains.
source: However, genetic knockout of SafA in S. typhimurium showed little difference in mouse virulence when compared to wild-type Salmonella strains (Folkesson et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SafD-dsc reveals a classic immunoglobulin-like fold, in which A-G strands form a β-sandwich fold with two β sheets packed against each other.
source: The SafD-dsc structure reveals a classic immunoglobulin-like fold, in which A-G strands form a β-sandwich fold with two β sheets packed against each other (Figure 2AB).
evidence: This is supported by the crystal structure data and illustrated in Figure 2AB.

claim: SafD is predicted to belong to the Afa/Dr poly-adhesin subfamily containing DraD, HdaB, AfaD, AafB and AggB.
source: Using Dali server (Holm and Rosenström, 2010), SafD is predicted to belong to the Afa/Dr poly-adhesin subfamily containing DraD (r.m.s.d. of 1.5 Å for 134 Cα atoms), HdaB (1.6 Å for 143 Cα atoms), AfaD (2.5 Å for 142 Cα atoms), AafB (1.1 Å for 129 Cα atoms) and AggB (1.5 Å for 133 Cα atoms) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis using Dali server and structural comparison data.

claim: AfaD adhesin/invasin, which shares 30% sequence homology with SafD, can recognize host receptor integrin α5/β1 and α5/β3.
source: In previous studies, it has been demonstrated that AfaD adhesin/invasin, which shares 30% sequence homology with SafD, can recognize host recetor integrin α5/β1 and α5/β3 (Cota et al., 2006; De Greve et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SafD-dsc structure harbors one highly negative charged patch that could constitute the binding site of the unknown host receptor.
source: Interestingly, SafD-dsc structure harbors one highly negative charged patch that could constitute the binding site of the unknown host receptor (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and is illustrated in Figure 2C. The use of 'could' indicates this is speculative.

claim: The P1-P5 residues (i.e. Gln9, Lys11, Val13, Ile15 and Phe17) of donor G strand interacts directly with the hydrophobic groove in SafD.
source: Similar to the published SafA-ANte structure (Remaut et al., 2006), the P1-P5 residues (i.e. Gln9, Lys11, Val13, Ile15 and Phe17) of donor G strand interacts directly with the hydrophobic groove in SafD (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by the crystal structure data and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: In P* position, Phe3 is no longer in direct interaction with SafD.
source: However, in P* position (a favored interaction that is thought to stabilize the exchanged product during DSE (Rose et al., 2008), Phe3 is no longer in direct interaction with SafD.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the SafD-dsc structure.

claim: The sidechain of Leu4 could interact with the hydrophobic core of SafD (termed P** pocket), mimicking the capping role of Phe3.
source: Instead, the sidechain of Leu4 could interact with the hydrophobic core of SafD (termed P** procket), mimicking the capping role of Phe3 (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and illustrated in figures. The use of 'could' indicates inference.

claim: The bulky hydrophobic residues in the positions 3 and 4 are conserved in SafA.
source: Consistently, the bulky hydrophobic residues in the positions 3 and 4 are conserved in SafA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The asymmetric unit (ASU) contains two SafD-dsc molecules.
source: The asymmetric unit (ASU) contains two SafD-dsc molecules.
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data.

claim: The superimposition of the SafD molecules shows interesting structural variations/flexibilities in LoopA-B on top of the P5 pocket.
source: The superimposition of the SafD molecules shows interesting structural variations/flexibilities in LoopA-B on top of the P5 pocket (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and illustrated in Figure 2D.

claim: The local environment around P5 is important for DSE.
source: Previous studies have shown that the local enviroment around P5 is important for DSE (Remaut et al., 2006; Verger et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Molecular dynamic (MD) simulation of E.coli pilin-Nte complex suggested that LoopA-B might play a regulatory role in DSE.
source: Supportively, molecular dynamic (MD) simulation of E.coli pilin-Nte complex suggested that this loop might play a regulatory role in DSE (Ford et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The SafD, SafA1, SafA2 and SafA3Nte have assembled into a thread-like shape with 26 Å in diameter and 136 Å in length/height.
source: The SafD, SafA1, SafA2 and SafA3Nte have assembled into a thread-like shape with 26 Å in diameter and 136 Å in length/height (Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on the crystal structure data and illustrated in figures.

claim: In ASU, three SafDAA-dsc molecules with an extended 'I'-like or a curvy 'L'-like architecture can be observed.
source: In ASU, three SafDAA-dsc molecules with an extended 'I'-like or a curvy 'L'-like architecture can be observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data and illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In the 'L'-architecture, SafA2 swings ~26 Å upward with its central axis in 90° angle with the rest of the structure.
source: In the 'L'-architecuture, SafA2 swings ~26 Å upward with its central axis in 90° angle with the rest of the structure.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the SafDAA-dsc crystal structure.

claim: The overall height of 'L'-like SafDAA-dsc (~110 Å) is significantly shorter than the 'I'-like architecture.
source: As a result, the overall height of 'L'-like SafDAA-dsc (~110 Å) is significantly shorter.
evidence: This is based on structural measurements from the crystal structure.

claim: The overall Ig-fold of SafD and SafA subunits is strictly conserved.
source: Structural comparisons among SafDAA-dsc structures show that: (1) The overall Ig-fold of SafD and SafA subunits is strictly conserved;
evidence: This is based on structural comparison analysis.

claim: The relative orientation between SafD and SafA1 is conserved.
source: (2) The relative orientation between SafD and SafA1 is also conserved. The r.s.m.d. values between different SafD-SafA1 molecules range from 0.5 to 0.8 Å for 290 Cα atoms.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison analysis with quantitative r.m.s.d. values.

claim: The intra-molecular interactions between SafD and SafA1 are mainly mediated by hydrogen bonds formed between Thr111, Phe14, Ala16 of SafD, and Gln143, Ser18, Asn6 of SafA1.
source: The intra-molecular interactions between SafD and SafA1 are mainly mediated by hydrogen bonds formed between Thr111, Phe14, Ala16 of SafD, and Gln143, Ser18, Asn6 of SafA1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B);
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There is no hydrogen bonding, electrostatic or hydrophobic interactions in between SafA1-SafA2.
source: (3) In marked contrast, there is no hydrogen bonding, electrostatic or hydrophobic interactions in between SafA1-SafA2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: SafA2 appears to be quite isolated and has the ability to move significantly to engage inter-molecular interaction as observed in the crystal.
source: The SafA2 appears to be quite isolated and has the ability to move significantly to engage inter-molecular interaction as observed in the crystal.
evidence: This is based on structural observations from the crystal structure.

claim: SafA-SafA is flexible and different SafA-SafA orientations can be observed by EM single-particle analysis.
source: Consistently, as demonstrated by EM single-particle analysis, SafA-SafA is indeed flexible and different SafA-SafA orientations can be observed (Salih et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The isomerization and torsion angles of Pro20 are important for the overall architecture and the flexibility of SafDAA-dsc.
source: (4) The isomerization and torsion angles of Pro20 are important for the overall architecture and the flexibility of SafDAA-dsc.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the SafDAA-dsc structure.

claim: The isomerization of proline residue is important for protein folding and diversity.
source: It has been reported that the isomerization of proline residue is important for protein folding and diversity (Lu et al., 2003; Nicholson and De, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Proline isomerization is important for pili assembly.
source: This is also the case in pili assembly (Li et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In between SafD and SafA1, Pro20 adopts a cis-configuration, enabling a kink in the subunit-subunit linker loop that allows the formation of intra-molecular hydrogen bonds.
source: In between SafD and SafA1, Pro20 adopts a cis-configuration, enabling a kink in the subunit-subunit linker loop that, in turn, allows the formation of intra-molecular hydrogen bonds (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Pro20 in between SafA1-SafA2 adopts a trans configuration, allowing SafA2 moving freely away from SafA1 as observed in 'I'- or 'L'-like architectures.
source: In comparison, Pro20 in between SafA1-SafA2 adopts a trans configuration, allowing SafA2 moving freely away from SafA1 as observed in 'I'- or 'L'-like architectures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Saf pili are required for intestinal colonization.
source: It has been reported that Saf pili are required for intestinal colonization (Carnell et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The recombinant SafDAA-dsc was functional and preserved the adhesive function of the Saf pilus.
source: Compared to control (i.e. the His-SH3 protein derived from human c-SRC that is exclusively expressed in cytoplasm, and hence is a good reference for non-specific interaction against IPEC-J2 cells), the cell adherence assay showed that the recombinant SafDAA-dsc was functional and preserved the adhesive function of the Saf pilus (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by cell adherence assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Saf pili are predicted to belong to a FGL pili subgroup, which is often associated with poly-adhesive activity.
source: Based on sequence and structural alignment, Saf pili are predicted to belong to a FGL pili subgroup, which is often associated with poly-adhesive activity (Zavialov et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on sequence and structural analysis, supported by a citation.

claim: When SafAA, SafD or SafA was incubated with IPEC-J2 cells, very little binding was observed.
source: When SafAA, SafD or SafA was incubated with IPEC-J2 cells, very little binding was observed (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by cell adherence assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: SafDAA yielded a strong binding signal with IPEC-J2 cells.
source: In marked contrast, SafDAA yielded a strong binding signal (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by cell adherence assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The removal of SafA subunit (SafDA) reduced host recognition.
source: In addition, the removal of SafA subunit (SafDA) reduced host recognition.
evidence: This is based on cell adherence assay data comparing SafDAA and SafDA.

claim: Bacteria can employ self-associated adhesins for initial cell-cell interaction, and subsequent microcolony and biofilm formation.
source: It is not uncommon that bacteria can employ self-associated adhesins for initial cell-cell interaction, and subsequent microcolony and biofilm formation (Garnett et al., 2012a; Garnett and Matthews, 2012; Heras et al., 2014; Klemm et al., 2006; Meng et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The SafDAA-dsc structures reveal two types of self-associating oligomerization in the crystal.
source: In this report, unexpectedly, the SafDAA-dsc structures reveal two types of self-associating oligomerization in the crystal (Figure 5BC).
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data and illustrated in Figure 5BC.

claim: In Type I dimerization, SafD and SafA1 interact with each other in a head-to-tail configuration mainly via inter-molecular hydrogen bonding involving residues Arg9, Thr7, Asn94 from SafD, and Glu8, Gln10 from SafA.
source: In Type I dimerization, SafD and SafA1 interact with each other in a head-to-tail configuration mainly via inter-molecular hydrogen bonding involving residues Arg9, Thr7, Asn94 from SafD, and Glu8, Gln10 from SafA (Figures 5B and 6A).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and illustrated in Figures 5B and 6A.

claim: When comparing SafA1 and different SafA2s (that do not form direct hydrogen bonds with SafD), a local side-chain reshuffle involving Glu8 could be observed in Type I dimerization.
source: Consistently, when comparing SafA1 and different SafA2s (that do not form direct hydrogen bonds with SafD), a local side-chain reshuffle involving Glu8 could be observed in Type I dimerization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison and illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: 'I'- and 'L'-like architecture are both observed in Type I dimer.
source: Consistently, 'I'- and 'L'-like architecture are both observed in Type I dimer (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on crystallographic data and illustrated in Figure 5B.

claim: In Type II dimerization, the SafD, SafA1 and SafA2 subunits make extensive interactions with the neighbour SafDAA-dsc via a '6–9'-like self-complementary architecture/surface.
source: In Type II dimerization, the SafD, SafA1 and SafA2 subuits make extensive interactions with the neighbour SafDAA-dsc via a '6–9'-like self-complementary architecture/surface (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and illustrated in Figure 5C.

claim: In Type II dimerization, the last SafA2 subunits have shifted up significantly to interact with the incoming SafD molecules.
source: In particular, the last SafA2 subunits have shifted up significantly to interact with the incoming SafD molecules.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of Type II dimerization.

claim: The morphologies of SafDAAs in Type II dimer are restricted to 'L'-like architecture.
source: As result, the morphologies of SafDAAs in this dimer are restricted to 'L'-like architecture (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and illustrated in Figure 5C.

claim: Type II dimerization displays few hydrogen bonds.
source: In marked contrast to Type I dimer, Type II dimerization displays few hydrogen bonds.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis comparing Type I and Type II dimers.

claim: SafDAA-SafDAA appears to engage each other via self-complementary surfaces controlled by Pro20.
source: The SafDAA-SafDAA appears to engage each other via self-complementary sufaces controled by Pro20 (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and illustrated in Figure 5A–C.

claim: Two types of head-to-tail-like engagements could give rise to a remarkable SafDAA trimer.
source: Taken together, these two types of head-to-tail-like engagements could give rise to a remarkable SafDAA trimer (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and illustrated in Figure 5D. The use of 'could' indicates inference.

claim: SAXS analysis suggested the existence of SafDAA-dsc monomer (79.7%), dimer (2.1%) and trimer (18.2%) in solution.
source: As shown in Figure 5E, the perfect match in crystal fitting with Chi2 value of 2.74 suggested the existence of SafDAA-dsc monomer (79.7%), dimer (2.1%) and trimer (18.2%) in solution (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is based on SAXS experimental data and analysis shown in Figure 5E and 5F.

claim: WT SafDAA-dsc and mutants behaved mainly as monomer in gel filtration column.
source: Consistent with SAXS analysis, WT SafDAA-dsc and mutants behaved mainly as monomer in gel filtraton column (Figure 6B), resemblance of the polymerization/depolymerization of self-associating Hap-Hap, Ag43-Ag43 interactions (Heras et al., 2014; Meng et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on SEC-MALS data shown in Figure 6B and supported by citations.

claim: WT SafDAA-dsc could undergo much higher oligomerization compared to mutants.
source: However, when comparing the oligomerization activities of these proteins, it is clear that WT SafDAA-dsc could undergo much higher oligomerizaiton (Figure 6B), whilst the self-associating activities were severely disrupted by the mutations of T7A/R9A/N94A, E8A/Q10A and P20A (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is based on SEC-MALS data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The self-associating activities were severely disrupted by the mutations of T7A/R9A/N94A, E8A/Q10A and P20A.
source: However, when comparing the oligomerization activities of these proteins, it is clear that WT SafDAA-dsc could undergo much higher oligomerizaiton (Figure 6B), whilst the self-associating activities were severely disrupted by the mutations of T7A/R9A/N94A, E8A/Q10A and P20A (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is based on SEC-MALS data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The beads coated with the recombinant SafDAA-dsc protein aggregated together to form clusters.
source: As shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1, the beads coated with the recombinant SafDAA-dsc protein aggregated together to form clusters.
evidence: This is based on latex beads assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The beads coated with SafD-dsc, SafA-dsc and BSA protein remained much isolated.
source: In comparison, the beads coated with SafD-dsc, SafA-dsc and BSA protein remained much isolated.
evidence: This is based on latex beads assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: E.coli cells with WT Saf, but not ∆SafA, showed significant increase of cell-cell interaction and colony formation visualized by light microscopy.
source: In agreement with beads aggregation observation, E.coli cells with WT Saf, but not ∆SafA, showed significant increase of cell-cell interaction and colony formation visualized by light microscopy (Figure 7CD).
evidence: This is based on cell aggregation assay data shown in Figure 7CD.

claim: When the perturbation/mutations were introduced to the SafDAA-SafDAA dimeric interfaces or in the proline residue of LoopG-A, the self-association suffered various degrees of disruption.
source: More importantly, when the perturbation/mutations were introduced to the SafDAA-SafDAA dimeric interfaces or in the proline residue of LoopG-A, the self-association suffered various degrees of disruption (Figure 7CD).
evidence: This is based on cell aggregation assay data shown in Figure 7CD.

claim: Double and multiple mutations (T7A/R9A/N94A and E8A/Q10A) displayed an aggravated effect with increased disruption in Saf-mediated biofilm formation.
source: Consistent with the results obtained in SEC-MALS and cell aggregation assay, doube and multiple mutations (T7A/R9A/N94A and E8A/Q10A) displayed an aggravated effect with increased disruption in Saf-mediated biofilm formation (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is based on biofilm formation assay data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: P20K mutation displayed disruptive effect on Saf-driven biofilm development.
source: As for Type II Saf pili dimerization, P20K mutation, which was engineered to restrict the proline flexibility and to disrupt the complementary architecture/surface in Type II dimerization, also displayed disruptive effect on Saf-driven biofilm development (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is based on biofilm formation assay data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The proline residue is frequently observed in the loop in between G- and A-strands, termed LoopG-A.
source: The proline residue is frequently observed in the loop in between G- and A-strands, termed LoopG-A.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis across different pili assemblies.

claim: The isomerization of Pro and the torsion angles of X-P-X (X for any amino acid) are important structural determinants for the overall architectures and functions in CFA/I fimbriae.
source: As shown in Figure 8C, the isomerization of Pro and the torsion angles of X-P-X (X for any amino acid) are indeed important structural determinants for the overall architectures and functions in CFA/I fimbriae (Li et al., 2009).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and supported by a citation.

claim: The initial interaction between subunit and the incoming Nte peptide in P5 pocket is thought to be the starting point of DSE process.
source: As previously characterized, the initial interaction between subunit and the incoming Nte peptide in P5 pocket is thought to be the starting point of DSE process (Remaut et al., 2006; Verger et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: MD simulation of PapD-PapGII complex suggested a regulatory role of LoopA-B.
source: MD simulation of in PapD-PapGII complex suggested a regulatory role of LoopA-B.
evidence: This is based on computational simulation studies.

claim: The Try13 sidechain of SafD might act as a molecular 'switch', regulating the access of incoming Nte peptide.

claim: Pro20 appears to play crucial roles in shaping the overall architecture and controlling the flexibility of Saf pili.
source: As revealed by SafDAA-dsc structure, Pro20 appears to play crucial roles in shaping the overall architecture and controlling the flexibility of Saf pili.

claim: The further variation of Pro20 isomerization and torsion angles will allow much versatile architecture of Saf pili that is necessary for the adherence and survival in different surfaces and environments.

evidence: This is a speculative claim based on structural observations.

claim: The isomerization of proline residue is frequently associated with protein folding.
source: Consistently, as observed elsewhere, the isomerization of proline residue is frequently associated with protein folding (Nicholson and De, 2011; Yuan et al., 1998).

claim: The isomerization switch of proline in LoopG-A allows CfaB-CafB to coil into a supra helical filament.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and illustrated in Figure 8C.

claim: Similar proline isomerization can be observed in E. coli PapA-PapA and its supra helical oligomerization.

claim: The SafDAA-dsc structure confirms the overall assembly of Saf pili, in which the major pilin SafA subunits, connected by the Nte peptides, is capped by a minor pilin SafD subunit.

claim: DraD and AfaD invasin subunits recognize the membrane bound integrins, possibly via the electrostatic protein:protein interaction.

claim: Bacterial pili can facilitate micro-colony and biofilm formation.

claim: Saf pili can mediate biofilm formation.

claim: The inter-cellular polymerization/depolymerization of H. influenzae self-associating Hap adhesin is an important mechanism to allow individual bacterium to traffic in/out of biofilm to survive in the host and to spread to other sites for colonization.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The self-associating inter-cellular oligomerization might represent a simple, but powerful strategy for bacterial aggregation and biofilm formation.
